question: Should OpenClaw accept the full agent-authored custom-widget security boundary in the first Workspaces landing, or narrow the initial product to trusted built-in widgets?
rationale: The six defects are mechanically repairable, but accepting unauthenticated approved asset serving and capability-bearing agent-authored browser code creates a lasting product and security ownership obligation that tests cannot decide.

options.title: Land full Workspaces after repair
options.body: Keep custom widgets, fix every blocker, and require exact-head lifecycle and security proof before merge.

options.title: Land trusted widgets first
options.body: Remove custom widgets and their unauthenticated route from this PR, then revisit that boundary separately.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the tracking issue open and defer this integration branch if maintainers do not want to own the boundary now.

recommendation.title: Land full Workspaces after repair
recommendation.body: Keep custom widgets, fix every blocker, and require exact-head lifecycle and security proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The live PR is assigned to this integration author, who shaped and hardened the final feature and security boundary.
